name: arc-enclosed-outline-fill
description: Use when ARC outlines enclose blank monochrome regions to recolor.

# Enclosed-outline fill (recurrence notes)

Use this rule when an ARC grid is mostly a uniform background and contains a contrasting-color outline that forms a closed boundary around one or more background-colored interiors. Recolor only the strictly enclosed interior cells; preserve the outline and all exterior background. A demonstrated recurrence uses fill color 4, regardless of the background or outline palette. Verify enclosure from the grid rather than assuming every near-rectangle is closed; do not fill open shapes or spaces that connect to the exterior.

## Confirmed instance: `task-66859c98`

A single demo established the behavior, and the test was solved correctly on the first submission after one demo request.

- Demo: 8×15, background 5 and outline 9. Closed outline enclosed a 4×5 interior (rows 3–6, columns 1–5, zero-based), which changed from 5 to 4. A second smaller enclosed interior (row 4, columns 11–13, zero-based) likewise changed from 5 to 4. All 9 outline cells and exterior 5s remained unchanged.
- Test: 23×10, background 2, outline 8. The closed rectangle spans rows 7–10 and columns 5–9 (zero-based); fill its interior rows 8–9, columns 6–8 with 4. Preserve the outline 8 and the surrounding 2s. This exact output was accepted.

The demo includes multiple closed components/regions, supporting filling all bounded background-colored interiors, not only one largest region. The distinguishing operation is an enclosed-region fill, not wholesale conversion of the outline or all cells of a certain color. Before submission, validate grid dimensions and confirm only interior cells were changed."
}
